Such an enjoyable 8km hike. The wind was frigid but the sun made it all worthwhile. So thankful for an open washroom, well groomed trail that was easy to follow. It had many wooden bridges including a covered bridge. We had brought snowshoes but found our hiking boots were all that was needed. The trail was very flat, packed crunchy snow. We enjoyed seeing the fishing huts as well as a kite skier gliding over the ice. The staff at the canoe rental area was very helpful in helping us to follow the trail after walking through the parking lot. You could smell the beautiful trees as you walked through the forest. We look forward to returning during the warmer months to enjoy it from a different season. What a beautiful and friendly area. You can see that a lot of people have been involved in creating an experience that can be enjoyed by many people all year round. Truly a gem that got my body moving and my spirit felt lifted.

This trail is ok, we did it with the kids, one of which was in a stroller. It's stroller friendly. I do recommend a jogging stroller with big wheels which is better for off-roading. The staff are friendly. They made this really nice covered wooden bridge which is close to the main building. There are large sections that are like grass fields, one of which is by a sand quarry. No shade on a sunny day which is really hard to walk in. Besides hearing trucks and loud metal banging, It was like a sandstorm up there. There is a covered patio there, we could not even use it. Everything was covered in sand. The wind was blowing sand in our faces and clothing. I could feel the sand gains between my teeth. Even though we were tired we had to get out of that area and keep hiking to a more sheltered area. This trail would probably be nicer on a cool day when there isn't much wind, or when the ground is more wet. Not sure I will visit this one again. Was very disappointed when I saw the sand quarry.  Also some clowns that hike were littering on the sides of the wooden walkways. Please don't be like that. There's lots of garbage cans along the trail. If you can carry your full water bottle in or walk your dog, it takes 0 effort to put the garbage into a bin. Please do not poop and scoop and then throw the poop filled bag into the forest, not smart at all.
